DESCRIPTION: Duplicate `task_id` values are never rejected, and several paths silently collapse them. `LoadBalancer.__init__` overwrites duplicates in `_task_idx`, `Allocation.get_assigned_models()` uses `list.index()` so it can only address the first matching row, and `Allocation.model_load()` rebuilds `{task_id: Task}`, so later duplicates overwrite earlier ones. I reproduced two tasks both named `dup` with demands `1000` and `9000`; the allocation matrix was `[[1], [1]]`, but `model_load('m', tasks)` returned `18000.0` because both rows were charged at the later task’s demand. This corrupts feasibility, cost, and audit semantics.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Enforce unique `task_id` values at construction or `LoadBalancer.__init__`, and make allocation accessors operate on validated row indices rather than ambiguous IDs.

LOCATION: [bench/dynamic_management.py#L236](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L236), [bench/dynamic_management.py#L352](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L352), [bench/dynamic_management.py#L377](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L377), [bench/dynamic_management.py#L424](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L424)  
DESCRIPTION: A non-finite capability value can be turned into an advantage, not just tolerated. `_compute_pool_max()` uses `np.max`, so a single `NaN` can taint a pool dimension. Then `CapabilityFingerprint.as_normalised_array()` does `np.where(pool_max > 0, raw / pool_max, 0.0)`; when `pool_max` is `NaN`, that branch falls back to `0.0`, and the later D-decay inversion turns it into `1.0`. I reproduced a two-model case where a model with `D_decay = nan` got role scores of `1.0` for every role and outranked a valid model. That is a specific, harmful failure mode beyond the general “missing NaN validation” concern.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Reject non-finite fingerprint fields on input, use explicit finite checks before normalisation, and never let fallback zeros pass through the D-decay inversion path.

DESCRIPTION: The PM-role invariant depends on a shared public dict with no defensive checks. `DynamicManager` passes `RoleAssignment.role_map` straight into `FailureHandler`, and `FailureHandler` stores it by reference. I verified `mgr.failure_handler.role_map is mgr.role_assignment.role_map` is `True`; after clearing that dict, `FailureHandler.should_abort()` returned `False` even though the system no longer had any PM at all. Because the map is shared and mutable, outside code or an internal bug can silently corrupt role assignment, failure handling, and allocation together.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Copy `role_map` at subsystem boundaries, keep it private, and assert “exactly one PM” in `FailureHandler.__init__()` and `should_abort()`.

DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager.check_dispatch_feasibility()` can approve dispatch to an excluded model. It accepts any `ModelSpec` and never checks whether that model is still in `failure_handler.active_models` or even belongs to the manager. I cleared the active set and still got `mgr.check_dispatch_feasibility(ModelSpec('m', ...), 10) == (True, 1.0)`. That means the manager’s own “safe to dispatch?” helper can bypass the recovery/exclusion layer and green-light work for models that have already been removed.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Reject feasibility checks for models outside the active pool, or change the API to take a managed `model_id` and resolve it internally from active state.

DESCRIPTION: Config vector validation is only a one-time check; afterwards the arrays stay mutable and aliased. `__post_init__()` validates `alpha_*` but does not copy or freeze them, and `get_alpha()` / `get_baseline()` return `np.asarray(...)`, which is the same object for ndarray inputs. I verified that mutating the original `alpha_pm` array after config construction changed the live config immediately: after setting the first element to `999`, `cfg.get_alpha(Role.PM)` returned `[999, 0.25, 0.25, 0.25]`. That lets post-validation mutation silently change PM/COL selection and expected-performance baselines mid-run.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Copy these arrays into private immutable storage during `__post_init__()`, and return defensive copies from the getters.
